meta.description: The n8n port of scripts/run_engine.py. Mirrors the reference: three separate outputs (human text, substantive handoff, control block), the same runtime envelope, the same three registries, the same retry/repair/dead-letter path, the same cost accounting, and transaction-local client scope on every write (D25). Built and proven against n8n 2.35.7 -- see docs/OPERATIONS.md 'n8n version' before deploying.

parameters.query: SELECT prompt_file, prompt_hash, content FROM engine_prompts WHERE engine = ($1::jsonb #>> '{}')::engine_id AND active

nodes.name: Prompt registry
nodes.notes: 010 / D23. No active row means PromptMissing: RUN_ENGINE never falls back to a stub (hard rule 7). The IF node below enforces that rather than letting an empty result flow on.

parameters.query: SELECT tag, required FROM engine_handoffs WHERE engine = ($1::jsonb #>> '{}')::engine_id AND mode = ($2::jsonb #>> '{}') AND active ORDER BY required DESC, tag

nodes.name: Handoff registry
nodes.notes: 013 / D24. Which substantive block this engine owes in this mode. Zero rows is HandoffMissing, not 'expect nothing' -- an unregistered mode would otherwise pass every check while producing no reasoning.

parameters.query: SELECT document, document_hash FROM orchestration_contracts WHERE schema_version = 'control_contract.v1' AND active

nodes.name: Contract registry
nodes.notes: 012 / D23. The JSON Schema the control block is validated against. ajv compiles THIS document; the Python reference compiles the same row with jsonschema, and test_contract_registry.py proves they agree.

nodes.name: Build request
nodes.notes: Byte-identical to scripts/run_engine.py build_user_prompt(). testing/test_n8n_parity.py compares both over a stored corpus covering non-ASCII, integral floats, empty containers and every JSON escape.

nodes.name: Open run
nodes.notes: Opens the run INSIDE a transaction that sets client scope (D25), and records engine_mode on the run itself so trg_engine_run_coherent can check client/mode coherence BEFORE the row exists (D27). Every parameter is a JSON literal unwrapped with #>> '{}' -- the binding form that is exact on n8n 2.11.4, which has no array branch (D32).

nodes.name: Call provider
nodes.notes: Calls the provider through helpers.httpRequest -- the Code node's vm2 sandbox has no fetch and no URL (D33) -- with the reference's retry semantics, which n8n's own retry cannot express (D29).

parameters.query:
SELECT set_client_scope(($1::jsonb #>> '{}')::uuid);
INSERT INTO cost_events (operation, model_role, model_name, entity_type, entity_id, run_id, workflow, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd, price_source, duration_ms, success, error_class)
SELECT 'ENGINE_RUN', ($2::jsonb #>> '{}'), ($3::jsonb #>> '{}'), 'client', ($4::jsonb #>> '{}'), ($5::jsonb #>> '{}')::uuid, ($6::jsonb #>> '{}'),
       (a->>'in_tok')::int, (a->>'out_tok')::int,
       p.cost_usd, p.price_source,
       (a->>'ms')::int, (a->>'ok')::boolean, a->>'error_class'
  FROM jsonb_array_elements($7::jsonb) a
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL price_call(($3::jsonb #>> '{}'), (a->>'in_tok')::int, (a->>'out_tok')::int,
                                ($8::jsonb #>> '{}')::numeric, ($9::jsonb #>> '{}')::numeric) p

nodes.name: Record attempts
nodes.notes: One cost_events row per PHYSICAL attempt, failures included -- a retry invisible in the cost table makes every measurement understate what a call costs, and D5 was decided on those numbers. Priced via the SQL price_call() over the model_prices registry (D30), because n8n cannot read config/model_prices.json.

nodes.name: Parse three outputs
nodes.notes: D24. The control block routes; the handoff is the reasoning. Line-oriented KEY: parsing with a key anchored at column zero, and nothing discarded -- _raw keeps the block verbatim, _preamble keeps text before the first key. Mirrors parse_handoff_block() in the reference.

nodes.name: Validate control
nodes.notes: 012 / D23. ajv over the stored document; test_contract_registry.py proves ajv and jsonschema reach identical verdicts AND blame identical fields over 26 control blocks.

nodes.name: Complete?
nodes.notes: A run is complete only with a valid control block AND every required handoff. A valid control block is not evidence that an engine did its work (D24). The false branch goes to repair, then dead-letter.

nodes.name: Dead letter
nodes.notes: raw_payload carries up to 8,000 characters of the failed response, which for a case run is labs, conditions and medications. It is kept -- debugging a dead letter without it is guesswork -- and it is SCOPED (D28). error_detail routinely contains commas, which is exactly what the JSON literal form protects: a bare string would be split into extra parameters (D32).

nodes.notes: Same shape as EngineResult in the reference, so a calling workflow reads the same fields the Python caller does.
